title: Conjecture 3
statement_text: For every positive integer $\ell$, there is a polynomial-time algorithm that given a planar near-Eulerian-triangulation $G$ with the outer face of length at most $\ell$ and a precoloring $\varphi$ of the vertices incident with the outer face decides whether $\varphi$ extends to a 4-coloring of $G$.
context_text: A planar near-Eulerian-triangulation is a plane graph in which all faces except possibly the outer one have length three and all vertices not incident with the outer face have even degree; equivalently, it is a patch (connected plane graph whose inner faces are triangles) that is 3-colorable, and when 2-connected its proper 3-coloring is unique up to permuting colors. A $4$-coloring is a proper coloring with $4$ colors, and a precoloring of the outer face extends if it is the restriction of a 4-coloring of $G$. Deciding 4-colorability of Eulerian triangulations of a fixed surface is the long-term motivation; the disk case with precolored boundary is the basic case of the usual cutting approach for graphs on surfaces. The authors give linear-time algorithms when the outer face is a cycle of length at most five, and when the outer face is a cycle of bounded length whose vertices all have odd degree and the precoloring uses only three colors. In general they only obtain a necessary topological condition (viability: the precoloring, together with the 3-coloring of $G$, must lift to a color- and hue-preserving homomorphism into the infinite triangular grid), shown sufficient when $G$ has an independent set $U$ disjoint from the outer cycle such that all inner faces of $G-U$ have length four. They conjecture that this condition combined with further ideas resolves the disk case in full.

title: Conjecture 4
statement_text: For every positive even integer $\ell$, there exists an integer $d$ such that the following claim holds. Let $G$ be a planar near-Eulerian-triangulation with the outer face bounded by a cycle $C$ of length $\ell$ and let $U$ be an independent set disjoint from $C$ such that $G-U$ is bipartite. Moreover, suppose that $G-U$ has a set $S$ of $d$ faces of length at least six such that there is no 4-cycle in $G-U$ separating a face of $S$ from the outer face, and for distinct faces $s_{1},s_{2}\in S$, the distance between $s_{1}$ and $s_{2}$ in $G-U$ is at least $d$ and there is no closed walk of length less than $\ell$ in $G-U$ separating both $s_{1}$ and $s_{2}$ from the outer face. Then any viable 4-coloring of $C$ extends to a 4-coloring of $G$.
context_text: A planar near-Eulerian-triangulation is a plane graph in which all faces except possibly the outer one have length three and all vertices not incident with the outer face have even degree; equivalently, it is a patch (connected plane graph whose inner faces are triangles) that is 3-colorable, and when 2-connected its proper 3-coloring is unique up to permuting colors. A $4$-coloring is a proper coloring with $4$ colors, and a precoloring of the outer face extends if it is the restriction of a 4-coloring of $G$. A hued graph is a graph with a fixed proper 3-coloring $\psi$ (its hue) with values in $\mathbb{Z}_3$; a dappled graph is a hued graph with in addition a proper 4-coloring $\varphi$ with values in $\mathbb{Z}_2^2$, and homomorphisms of dappled graphs must preserve edges, hues and colors. The dappled triangular grid $T$ has vertex set $\mathbb{Z}^2$, $(i_1,j_1)$ adjacent to $(i_2,j_2)$ iff $(i_2-i_1,j_2-j_1)\in\{\pm(1,0),\pm(0,1),\pm(1,1)\}$, hue $(i+j)\bmod 3$ and color $(i\bmod 2,j\bmod 2)$. A 4-coloring $\varphi$ of a connected hued graph $C$ (here the outer cycle with the hue inherited from the 3-coloring of $G$) is viable if the resulting dappled graph has a homomorphism to $T$; equivalently, the induced map of $C$ to $K_3\times K_4$ (drawn as a triangulation of the torus whose universal cover is $T$) is a contractible closed walk. The authors show that viability is a necessary condition for a precoloring of the outer face to extend, and that it is checkable in linear time. Faces of $G-U$ (the plane graph obtained by deleting $U$) have even length since $G-U$ is bipartite; the authors prove that viability is sufficient when all inner faces of $G-U$ have length four. The conjecture asserts that it is also sufficient in a 'sufficiently generic' situation where $G-U$ has many long faces that are far apart and not separated from the outer face by short cycles or walks. It is proposed as a step towards the companion conjecture that for every fixed $\ell$ precoloring extension of an outer face of length at most $\ell$ in planar near-Eulerian-triangulations is decidable in polynomial time.
